chunks: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hasani raised it (the chain), and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari, who raised it (the chain), said:
When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was struck, the visitors gathered around him, and it was said to him: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, make your bequest!' So he said: 'Fold the pillow for me.'
Then he said: 'Praise be to Allah as is His right, following His command, and I praise Him as He loves, and there is no god but Allah, the One, the Unique, the Eternal, as He has described Himself.'

O people! Every person will encounter during his flight that which he flees from, and death is the driver of the soul toward it, and fleeing from it is to meet it. How many days I spent searching through them for the hidden secret of this matter, but Allah — Mighty is His mention — refused except to keep it hidden. How far away is hidden knowledge!

As for my bequest: do not associate anything with Allah — Majestic is His praise — and as for Muhammad (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family), do not waste his Sunnah. Establish these two pillars and kindle these two lamps, and you will be free of blame as long as you do not stray. Every person carries the burden of his own effort, and the Merciful Lord has lightened it from the ignorant. A Merciful Lord, a Most-Knowing Imam, and a straight Religion.

Yesterday I was your companion, today I am a lesson for you, and tomorrow I shall part from you. If the footing holds firm at this slippery place, that is the goal; and if the foot slips, then we were in the shades of branches, the shelter of winds, and under the shadow of a cloud whose mass dissolved in the atmosphere and whose traces faded on the earth.

I was only a neighbor; my body was your neighbor for a few days, and soon you will be left with an empty body from me — still after movement, and silent after speech. Let my stillness, the dimming of my gaze, and the quietness of my limbs be your admonishment, for that is more admonishing for you than an eloquent speaker. I bid you farewell as one expecting reunion. Tomorrow you will witness my days, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic — will unveil my secrets, and you will come to know me after my place is empty and another stands in my place.

If I survive, then I am the guardian of my own blood; and if I perish, then perishing is my appointed meeting; and if I forgive, then forgiving is for me a nearness (to Allah) and for you a good deed. So forgive and overlook. Would you not love that Allah should forgive you? What a remorse upon every heedless one — that his own lifetime should become an argument against him, or his days lead him to misery.
May Allah make us and you among those who are not held back from obedience to Allah by worldly desire, nor visited after death by divine punishment — for truly we belong to Him and are with Him.
Then he turned toward al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: 'O my son, a strike in place of a strike, and do not sin.'

key_terms.الصَّمَد: Al-Samad — the Eternal, Self-Sufficient; one of God's most exalted names from Quran 112:2
key_terms.الْأَجَل: The appointed time of death; the divinely determined moment of death
key_terms.الْعَمُودَيْن: The two pillars — tawhid (divine unity) and adherence to the Prophet's Sunnah
key_terms.الْمَزَلَّة: A slippery place; metaphor for the dangers and trials of this world
key_terms.الْمِصْبَاحَيْن: The two lamps — metaphors for the Quran and the Sunnah (or tawhid and wilaya)
key_terms.سُنَّة: The prophetic practice/tradition of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.هَيْهَاتَ: Far be it! How distant! — exclamation of impossibility or remoteness
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Bequest, final testament — the solemn dying instructions of the Imam
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الدَّم: The guardian of blood — the one who has the right to demand retribution or pardon

ai.seo_question: What were the last words and final testament of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib before his death?
ai.summary: This is the final testament (wasiyya) of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), delivered after he was mortally wounded by Ibn Muljam's strike during the Fajr prayer of Ramadan 40 AH. As visitors gathered around the dying Imam, he requested a pillow, then delivered this profound bequest touching on monotheism, the inevitability of death, the obligation to uphold God's unity and the Prophet's Sunnah, and a meditation on the transience of life. The Imam concluded with a merciful instruction to his son al-Hasan (AS) not to retaliate beyond measure.
